history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was an initiative by Harvard University aimed at advancing our understanding of aerosol behavior in the stratosphere. This scientific endeavor, led by Frank Keutsch and his collaborators, was intended to refine computer models that assess the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering—not to implement geoengineering itself or to cool the planet. The proposed experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola operating at high altitudes, releasing a minuscule amount of calcium carbonate for measurement purposes. Importantly, a 2021 platform test in Sweden was focused solely on hardware, with the SCoPEx Advisory Committee advocating for a pause pending societal engagement, ensuring transparency and public accountability. As of March 2024, Harvard announced that the project would no longer be pursued, redirecting the platform towards research that prioritizes scientific integrity and climate justice without resorting to unverified geoengineering methods. We must remain diligent in advocating for genuine climate action that addresses emissions and promotes equitable governance, rather than relying on potential moral hazards that could delay essential mitigation efforts.
